negative_findings.description: No Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE or Finastra page naming a North Macedonian bank as a published customer was found in this pass. The only evidence linking Temenos T24 and Oracle Mantas to Stopanska Banka came from a third-party technographics aggregator, not from the vendors themselves.
negative_findings.result_summary: Vendor-side confirmation of MK core-banking installs is absent from open search results; only aggregator claims exist.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Core-banking vendor identity is the single highest-value competitor fact for this market; relying on an unverified aggregator risks propagating a wrong vendor-bank pairing.

negative_findings.description: Neither Diebold Nixdorf nor NCR Atleos surfaced any press release or case study naming a North Macedonian bank; the only MK ATM-vendor evidence found was second-hand, via Printec's local country page describing NCR SelfServ deployment at HALKBANK AD Skopje.
negative_findings.result_summary: OEM newsrooms appear silent on MK; the channel partner (Printec) is the disclosing party.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that in MK the ATM/self-service supply chain is visible mainly at the integrator/distributor layer, so collection must be aimed at channel partners rather than OEM newsrooms.

negative_findings.description: Macedonian-language queries using generic vendor-marketing vocabulary ('студија на случај', 'успешна приказна', 'имплементација решение банка') returned academic methodology pages, government fintech-strategy documents and non-banking ERP success stories rather than vendor case studies naming banks.
negative_findings.result_summary: MK-language vendor case-study genre appears thin to non-existent; local vendors publish wins as news items and LinkedIn posts, not as case studies.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language collection strategy must be re-tuned toward 'соопштение', 'партнерство', 'нова услуга', 'во соработка со', and bank brand names instead of case-study vocabulary.

negative_findings.description: No Mastercard or Visa press release naming a North Macedonian bank partnership or MK tokenization/wallet launch was found; scheme newsrooms returned only global and Western-European announcements.
negative_findings.result_summary: Scheme-level MK announcements not visible in indexed English press for the searched period.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Scheme press is normally a reliable pointer to issuer-side technology partners; its absence means MK scheme news likely appears only in local media or bank press rooms.

negative_findings.description: Root/landing URLs for casys.com.mk, duna.mk, and the newsroom/case-study index paths for Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Temenos and Oracle were inferred from company identity and standard site structure rather than clicked through in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Several candidate URLs are pattern-inferred and must be liveness-checked by the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents false confidence: these are plausible entry points, not confirmed-reachable pages.

coverage_gaps.description: Only a handful of MK banks (Komercijalna, Stopanska, Halkbank) produced any vendor-side evidence. NLB Banka Skopje, Sparkasse Bank Makedonija, ProCredit, Silk Road Bank, TTK Banka, Centralna Kooperativna Banka, UNIBanka, Capital Bank and the Development Bank of North Macedonia are entirely uncovered on the vendor-reference axis.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run one systematic vendor-reference sweep per bank brand (mk and en spellings, plus group parents NLB, Steiermärkische, ProCredit, Ziraat, Halkbank TR), since group-level vendor deals often cascade to the MK subsidiary.

coverage_gaps.description: AML/compliance, fraud, card-issuance/personalisation (IDEMIA, G+D, Thales), HSM/security, instant-payments and clearing infrastructure vendors were only touched indirectly; no dedicated sweep was done for MK-named references in these segments.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Dedicated per-segment vendor sweeps, including the vendor lists behind the national payment infrastructure (KIBS, MIPS/instant payments) which sit adjacent to this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Public-procurement and tender records (e-nabavki.gov.mk) and state-owned/Development Bank IT tenders were not searched, although these publish awarded supplier names and contract values — often the only hard confirmation of a vendor-bank relationship.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a procurement-portal sweep keyed to bank and vendor names; treat awarded-contract notices as the corroborating layer for vendor marketing claims.

coverage_gaps.description: Albanian-language sources were not searched at all, despite a large Albanian-speaking market segment in MK and vendors (e.g. CaSys' Albanian fintech partner Rubicon) operating across the MK-AL corridor.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add sq-language queries (bankë, zgjidhje, partneritet, kartë) and Albanian-market vendor press to the next pass.

coverage_gaps.description: Findings cluster on recent (2023-2026) digital-channel launches; older core-banking and card-platform selections that still define incumbency were not traced.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search web archives and older vendor newsroom pages (2010-2020) for MK bank names to reconstruct incumbency and replacement cycles.

brief: Vendor-published customer references naming North Macedonian banks are real but sparse and asymmetrically distributed: the richest disclosures come from regionally-embedded suppliers with Skopje operations (Printec, Nextsense, ASEE/Payten, CaSys, G+D Netcetera) rather than from global OEM newsrooms, which were silent on MK in this pass. The strongest confirmed pointers are Printec's MK country page (NCR SelfServ ATMs at HALKBANK AD Skopje), Nextsense's announcement of Komercijalna Banka's digital onboarding platform, and Entrust's Google Pay push-provisioning release for the same bank; core-banking attribution (Temenos T24, Oracle Mantas AML at Stopanska Banka) currently rests only on a third-party technographics aggregator and needs vendor- or bank-side corroboration. Macedonian-language 'case study' vocabulary is largely unproductive — local wins are published as news items, association coverage (ecommerce.mk) and LinkedIn posts — so collection should target 'соопштение/партнерство/во соработка со' plus bank brand names, and exploit high-signal indirect sources such as app-store package IDs and vendor partner directories. Priority next moves: a per-bank sweep across the eight uncovered MK banks, per-segment sweeps for AML/card-issuance/HSM vendors, and a public-procurement cross-check to harden vendor-bank pairings.
